messages:
Maria: quick thought — want to propose an experiment to reduce noisy GPU pages while keeping fast handoff to ticketing for persistent issues :thinking_face:
Aj: ok lay it out, what are we changing?
Maria: current problem: short flares (30s-2m) cause pages, but most resolve; we want to avoid waking oncalls for those. long incidents still need pages. idea: add a short suppression layer + grouping + a soft 'handoff' rule to create tickets after X minutes. run this as a canary on us-west GPU pool first.
Lee: 👍 can we quantify? what metrics/alerts will change?
Maria: baseline: pages/day ~ 12 (gpu-flare alerts), tickets/day ~ 3, MTTR ~ 35m. target: pages drop >=50% without increasing true-incident MTTR by >10%.
Oliver: how will suppression work technically? simple cooldown or more stateful?
Maria: proposal: 3-tier behavior:
  1) short bursts (<3m) => group + suppress paging, emit a low-severity ticket event.
  2) sustained (>3m and <12m) => escalate to ticket and add a 3-minute delay before paging to let grouping collect context.
  3) sustained (>12m) or severity label (disk/net errors) => immediate page.
Tanvi: sounds reasonable. need safe defaults so we don't miss regressions. also add circuit-breaker: if p99 latency spikes > 2x baseline then page immediately.
Aj: can we express this with Prometheus alerts + Alertmanager routing? maybe using `for` and grouping labels. example rule I sketched:
```yaml
- alert: GPU_Bursting_Flare
  expr: increase(gpu_error_count[5m]) > 0 and avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[1m]) > 0.8
  for: 30s
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    handoff_phase: burst
- alert: GPU_Sustained_Flare
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[5m]) > 0.85
  for: 6m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
    handoff_phase: sustained
- alert: GPU_Critical_Flare
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization[5m]) > 0.9 or increase(gpu_error_count[1m]) > 5
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: page
    handoff_phase: critical
```
Lee: alertmanager route idea: route burst->no-page but annotate & create ticket; sustained->ticket + delayed page route; critical->page. we can use `group_interval` to coalesce bursts into one notification.
Maria: also adding an adaptive backoff: if the pool has >3 flares in 1h, shorten the suppression so we escalate faster (sign of real problem).
Tanvi: schedule for canary: us-west1/gpu-pool-b for 72h, then compare signal. canary metrics to track: pages, tickets, mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA), mean time to resolve (MTTR), customer-facing error rate.
Oliver: can we simulate with historical alerts? I ran a 48h replay on last month's data and got: pages reduced by 62%, tickets increased by 8%, MTTR for true incidents +6%. logs: most suppressed bursts were <90s. I can share the notebook.
Maria: please link the replay and the Grafana dashboards in the thread.
Oliver: replay notebook: <https://playbooks.redwood.net/replays/gpu-flare-replay-2026-02-14>
Oliver: quick grafana for canary: <https://grafana.redwood.net/d/gpu-flare-canary?orgId=1&var-pool=us-west1>
Aj: two operational concerns: 1) runbook needs a clear handoff — if ticket auto-generated, include diagnostic snapshot + KV cache stats + last 5 requests. 2) oncall should be able to opt-out of suppression per rotation.
Tanvi: runbook snippet suggestion: include command to force page: `curl -XPOST https://alertmanager.../api/v1/silences`?? actually that's silence. better: `curl -XPOST /api/v1/alerts -d '{"labels": {"severity":"page","force":"true"}}'` — included in the playbook.
Maria: good — also add a short checklist to ticket template: "did suppression hide a signal? add /annotate with steps"
Lee: stakeholder question: will this affect billing/auto-scaling triggers? sometimes pages are correlated with autoscaler churn. ensure we keep autoscaler alarms separate and always page on node provisioning failures.
Maria: agreed — add label `infrastructure=true` for those alerts to bypass suppression.
Aj: one more: we should add a postmortem sampling rule: if a ticket converted to page within 24h, auto-create a postmortem stub flagged `handoff=true` for SRE review.
Tanvi: timeline: implement alert rules + alertmanager route + runbook updates in `infra/alerting` branch, run canary for 72h starting Friday 08:00 PST, then quick sync Monday.
Maria: volunteers: Oliver -> run replays & dashboards; Lee -> alertmanager route changes; Aj -> runbook + postmortem automation; Tanvi -> coordinate canary schedule and pager opt-out UI toggle. I'll own rollout and final decision.
PagerBot: scheduled: canary-start 2026-03-20T08:00:00-08:00 for 72h (us-west1/gpu-pool-b). reminders set. :white_check_mark:
Aj: small nit — add a short log sample to the ticket template (last 200 lines). reduces context switching.
Oliver: added sample and notebook link to the infra/alerting PR -> <https://git.redwood/infrastructure/alerting/pulls/87>
Maria: thanks all. if nobody raises major objections by EOD tomorrow we'll merge and run. please keep thread updated with any simulation anomalies. :rocket:
